analysis: Examined base lines 354-709 of docs/reference/configuration.md and the file_changes map. The range map is complete, but the patch excerpt is truncated. Changed ranges are base 3/567/583-584 and head 3/371/568/584-590. Head 371 adds DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE, which defaults to ~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json and is read by ProviderCore/Service/VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift. It stores fully verified managed-load weight hashes bound to each file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime. Startup registration reuses a matching record instead of re-hashing. Base 583-584 says discovery is hash-free and fresh pre/post-load verification keeps its rules. The head 584-590 rewrite is not visible, so how far this caching relaxes fresh verification is unknown. Security relevance: T-012/T-027 (operator weight substitution, A-004) and TB-003. The operator owns ~/.darkbloom, so 'owner-only' permissions do not protect against ADV-001. If VerifiedWeightHashStore records are not authenticated by a key the operator cannot read (SE/keychain-rooted MAC), an operator could forge a record. They would pair substituted weights' stat tuple with a trusted hash, and the provider would publish a false weightHash at startup. T-041 also binds cache entries to the verified weightHash. A stat tuple is also not proof of content against a root-capable operator who can preserve or restore metadata on a clone. The weight hash is already partly self-reported/fail-open per T-012/SEC-007, so whether this is a regression depends on unsupplied code. The open questions are: is the record integrity-protected, and is it bound to the binary/process identity? Also, does post-load verification still re-hash, or does the record now bypass it before identity publication? The source was not supplied, so this is recorded as a question, not a finding. Base 567 / head 568 (DARKBLOOM_MEMORY_AVAILABILITY) changed only by an unseen edit; it is an availability-only control. The other visible rows (prefix-cache, MiMo, Qwen4, Bonsai, GPT-OSS controls) are unchanged base context. They are consistent with the T-041 TTL ≤1800 rule and the kill-switch semantics.
